title: LLM See, LLM Do: Guiding Data Generation to Target Non-Differentiable Objectives
findings: Finetuning language models on synthetic data, even with prompts that are neutral in domain, leads to noticeable and non-trivial changes in their social bias profiles, including religious bias. The study found that a model's stereotype score for religion can change significantly after being trained on distilled data, and the direction of this change (i.e., whether the bias increases or decreases) is not always intuitive or predictable.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured social bias, specifically the stereotype scores associated with the category of 'religion' in language models. This was assessed using fill-in-the-blank style association tests (StereoSet, CrowS-Pairs) and bias in question-answering scenarios (BBQ).
